title: Shared Selective Persistent Memory for Agentic LLM Systems
gist: An EMNLP paper by Sanjana Pedada, Aditya Dhavala and Neelraj Patil introduces 'shared selective persistent memory', which keeps only four reusable context categories (task specs, data schemas, tool configurations, output constraints) and discards session reasoning traces, lifting task completion to 96% versus 79% with no memory and 71% with full conversation history. It is deployed in a collaborative workspace where LLM agents build git-versioned dashboards and reports over CSV, SQL, REST and MCP connectors, with a zero-token data refresh path that cuts recurring-update task time 14x and summary-driven generation that cuts per-invocation token cost 97x.

insights.claim: Persisting a coding agent's entire conversation history actively degrades task completion — 71% with full history versus 79% with no memory at all — because stale reasoning traces bias the agent.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Undercuts the 'infinite context window / dump everything in' pitch that long-context model vendors and memory startups sell; buyers should demand selectivity benchmarks, not context length.
insights.quote: naive full-history persistence actively degrades task completion by biasing the agent with stale reasoning traces, while selective memory outperforms both extremes

insights.claim: Selecting and retaining only reusable context raised task completion to 96%, versus 79% for a memoryless baseline and 71% for full-history persistence, across three enterprise deployment scenarios.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A ~17-point completion gain from memory engineering alone suggests agent reliability is currently gated by context curation, not model capability — value accrues to the orchestration layer.
insights.quote: shared selective persistent memory achieves 96% task completion (vs. 79% without memory and 71% with full history)

insights.claim: The proposed memory architecture retains exactly four categories of context — task specifications, data schemas, tool configurations, and output constraints — and throws away session-specific reasoning traces.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A concrete, copyable taxonomy for anyone building agent memory; vendors whose 'memory' is undifferentiated embedding recall are a generation behind this framing.
insights.quote: four categories of reusable context—task specifications, data schemas, tool configurations, and output constraints—while discarding session-specific reasoning traces
insights.locator: We introduce shared selective persistent memory

insights.claim: Every fresh agentic coding session is framed as starting from zero, discarding the configuration choices, domain constraints, data schemas and tool-use patterns that made prior sessions productive.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Names the specific waste in enterprise agent deployments — respecification cost — which is the wedge any agent-memory product must attack to justify pricing.
insights.quote: each session starts from zero, discarding the configuration choices, domain constraints, data schemas, and tool-use patterns that made previous sessions productive
insights.locator: Agentic LLM systems that generate code

insights.claim: A zero-token data refresh mechanism decouples generated programs from runtime data so recurring data updates require no LLM re-invocation at all, cutting task time by 14x.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Recurring reporting workloads may consume far fewer inference tokens than per-refresh pricing models assume — a headwind to seat-plus-token revenue forecasts for agent platforms.
insights.quote: A complementary zero-token data refresh mechanism eliminates LLM re-invocation entirely for recurring data updates (14×task time reduction)
insights.locator: A complementary zero-token data refresh mechanism

insights.claim: Feeding the model data summaries instead of raw data reduced per-invocation token cost by 97x.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Two orders of magnitude of cost sits in prompt-construction discipline, so inference spend per enterprise agent task is highly compressible and not a durable moat for compute-heavy vendors.
insights.quote: summary-driven generation reduces per-invocation token cost by 97×versus raw data injection

insights.claim: Git-backed versioning with draft isolation lets users explore modifications and restore any prior artifact state without re-invoking the model.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Undo-without-inference is a design pattern that turns model calls into a scarce resource; watch for it becoming standard in agent UX and further deflating per-task token demand.
insights.quote: Git-backed versioning with draft isolation enables users to explore modifications risk-free and restore to any prior state without re-invoking the model.

themes.theme: Shared workspaces as the enterprise unit

insights.claim: Selective memory is packaged into transferable workspaces that move across users under role-based access control, letting teams reuse accumulated context instead of respecifying it.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Turns agent memory into a shareable, permissioned asset — the kind of account-level artifact that creates switching costs and seat expansion in enterprise AI tooling.
insights.quote: workspaces encapsulating selective memory can be transferred across users with role-based access control

insights.claim: The architecture is already implemented in a deployed collaborative workspace platform where LLM agents produce, edit and maintain git-versioned interactive dashboards, structured reports and data-driven documents.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Signals that agent-generated BI artifacts are past prototype stage, putting pressure on incumbent dashboard and reporting vendors.
insights.quote: a deployed collaborative workspace platform where LLM agents produce, edit, and maintain git-versioned artifacts

insights.claim: The platform ingests heterogeneous data through four connector types — CSV upload, SQL, REST APIs and MCP servers — with MCP treated as a first-class enterprise data path alongside SQL.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Further evidence MCP is consolidating as the standard agent-to-data interface, which matters for anyone betting on proprietary connector ecosystems.
insights.quote: multiple connector types (CSV upload, SQL, REST APIs, and MCP servers)

insights.claim: Results were replicated on four public datasets, with the zero-token refresh mechanism succeeding in 12 of 12 trials, arguing the gains are not artifacts of the three enterprise deployments.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Clean-sweep replication raises the odds the technique diffuses quickly into competing agent platforms, shortening any first-mover advantage.
insights.quote: A replication on four public datasets confirms generalizability, with zero-token refresh succeeding in 12/12 trials.
insights.locator: A replication on four public datasets

themes.theme: Adjacent agent-tooling research on the page

insights.claim: A companion research item argues that hand-built agent evaluation scenarios do not scale across tool ecosystems and produce static benchmarks that cannot track evolving APIs, proposing that tool specifications themselves — function names, descriptions and typed parameters — be used to generate test scenarios.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Agent benchmark decay is an under-priced risk: procurement teams relying on static tool-use leaderboards may be buying against stale evidence.
insights.quote: Constructing such scenarios by hand demands deep domain expertise, does not scale across tool ecosystems, and produces static benchmarks that cannot track evolving APIs.
insights.locator: Evaluating AI agents that use external tools

insights.claim: Older on-device work on False-Trigger-Mitigation frames per-invocation models and a single all-invocation model as both sub-optimal, because per-invocation memory cost grows with the number of invocation options.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The same memory-cost-versus-specialization tradeoff recurring from 2023 speech models to 2026 agent memory suggests a durable design constraint in on-device AI worth watching in Apple's silicon roadmap.
insights.quote: the memory cost for the former approach grows
insights.locator: Suppressing unintended invocation of the device

insights.claim: The published record carries no author byline in its metadata, with the named researchers Sanjana Pedada, Aditya Dhavala and Neelraj Patil appearing only inside the body text.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Attribution lives in the text rather than structured fields, so downstream pipelines tracking researcher moves between labs need body-text parsing, not metadata.
insights.quote: AuthorsSanjana Pedada, Aditya Dhavala, Neelraj Patil
insights.locator: Shared Selective Persistent Memory for Agentic LLM Systems
